card.name: Words introducing a drug-use instruction
card.fires_on: The word right after a caution or heading phrase in drug labels, mainly "when" after "caution should be exercised", and "of" after "Co-administration". It sits where the drug being given comes next.

modes.label: Caution when
modes.description: "when" after "caution should be exercised" in the nursing mother section.
modes.example: Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised<< when>> this product is administered to a nursing woman

modes.label: Co-administration of
modes.description: "of" right after "Co-administration" in interaction text, before a drug name.
modes.example: Lipid Lowering Drugs Co-administration<< of>> cholestyramine or colest

modes.label: Instruction verbs
modes.description: A verb that opens an instruction or section, such as Use or Avoid, or "add" in an instruction.
modes.example: .<< Avoid>> the use of piroxicam capsules

card.writes: The promoted tokens are mostly Chinese words meaning "applied to", "replace" or "facing", so there is no clear effect on English drug text.
card.plain: It marks the small word that comes just before the label says which drug is being given or used.
